extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in the Norma Khouri case, literary hoaxes, and nonfiction authenticity
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and signals for evaluating the truthfulness, provenance, and ethical presentation of purported nonfiction/memoir work, illustrated by the Norma Khouri / Forbidden Love hoax. Useful for readers, journalists, and publishers checking claims in life‑story narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purported factual claims / truthfulness of narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: The book purported to describe the honor killing of her best friend in Jordan and later was exposed as a literary hoax in 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claims presented as factual as testable assertions: seek corroborating evidence (documents, independent witnesses, official records). Anti‑pattern: accepting sensational personal claims without verification. Example: Khouri's central narrative was later shown not to be true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of the author's stated residency and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Khouri was revealed not to be living in Jordan during 1993–1995 (the timeframe of Forbidden Love), but in Chicago with her family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify an author's stated whereabouts and timelines against available records (e.g., travel records, public documents, contemporaneous accounts). Inconsistencies between claimed lived experience and documentary evidence undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of firsthand experience and depth of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Khouri had not lived in Jordan since early childhood, except for a three‑week stay during which she apparently researched the background for her book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether brief visits or secondhand research suffice to justify claims of lived experience. Criteria: length/intensity of immersion, primary sources consulted, and methodological transparency about research methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of factual errors and attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The book attracted criticism from Jordanian writers and groups regarding numerous errors, which contributed to its exposure as a hoax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check factual assertions (cultural, geographic, legal, biographical) for mistakes; numerous small errors are a red flag for fabrication or poor research. Publishers and reviewers should flag and correct factual inaccuracies before and after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about fictionalisation / disclosure of 'literary licence'
rubrics_metrics.description: Khouri later admitted she took 'literary licence' with the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elements are fictionalized or composite, authors and publishers should explicitly label the work (e.g., novel, roman à clef, based on true events) so readers are not misled. Failure to disclose fictionalisation transforms a work marketed as nonfiction into a potential hoax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher vetting and due diligence for nonfiction claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Random House published the book; its publication became complicated when author background and claims were disputed and she had been sponsored under a nomination category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should perform fact‑checking, especially for sensational nonfiction: verify author credentials, timeline claims, and supporting evidence. Consider heightened scrutiny where immigration, awards, or grants may be affected by claimed status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with requests for documentation and transparency in investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Khouri said she would cooperate with all requests to provide documentation after the allegations surfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disputes arise, credible authors should provide documentation (records, contacts) to substantiate claims. Non‑cooperation or evasiveness is a negative signal; prompt, verifiable cooperation can help resolve doubts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of financial interests / payments and potential motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Khouri claimed she did not receive payment or royalties for writing the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and disclose financial relationships and gains connected to a claimed true story, as financial incentives can be a motive for fabrication. Investigators and readers should consider payment/royalty information when assessing motive and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential legal, ethical, and reputational consequences of false claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusations surrounding Khouri included prior investigations (e.g., alleged defrauding of an elderly neighbor) and immigration review; the hoax resulted in widespread media exposure and reputational damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that presenting false nonfiction can trigger legal inquiries, immigration/award implications, and significant reputational harm. Evaluators should be alert to related allegations that may bear on the trustworthiness of the author.
